our_title: k-way FM reuses a stale domain count after its fallback adds parts, overflowing load arrays
ran: Pristine 7.0.17 ASan/UBSan (32-bit Gnum). Public API: `./GRA-02/gra02pub 4 'rf{bal=0.00001}'` -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 ... #0 kgraphMapFmTablGet kgraph_map_fm.c:129 #1 kgraphMapFm kgraph_map_fm.c:1320'. Internal: `./GRA-02/gra02int 24 64 2` -> 'heap-buffer-overflow ... 12 bytes after 24-byte region'. Patched: gra02pub -> 'ret=0 maxpart=3'; gra02int 16/4/1, 16/16/2, 24/64/2 -> ret=0 with domnnbr refreshed 1->4, 2->16, 2->64; passes under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL (kgraphMapFmCheck + kgraphCheck, no internal error).
severity_note: Agrees with the review: memory corruption reachable from a user strategy string through the public SCOTCH_graphMap (e.g. 'rf{bal=...}'); growth beyond the 32-bit |8 malloc slack corrupts the heap.
evidence: 7.0.17: `const Gnum domnnbr = grafptr->m.domnnbr;` (:997) is never refreshed; after `kgraphMapSt (grafptr, strat)` (:1040) the comment at :1047 even says 'domnnbr has changed after mapping' yet memReallocGroup still uses the old domnnbr; kgraphMapFmTablGet then reads comploaddlt/comploadmax past their end.
review_accuracy: Accurate. The review's two suggested fixes are both viable; 'Re-read domnnbr/domntab after the fallback' is the one implemented. The review did not mention the leaked fallback strategy or the ignored kgraphMapSt return value, both fixed here.
first_pass_critique: Correct status/method/evidence and the preferred option matches. Its stale-use list (savetab sizing ~1460, write-back ~1831) is right and both are covered by refreshing domnnbr early. Its sketch left the memReallocGroup-failure path leaking comploadmax; the committed fix frees it there too.

fix_options.label: Refresh domnnbr after the fallback (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Make domnnbr a mutable local, re-read grafptr->m.domnnbr after the fallback kgraphMapSt, reallocate+refill the imbalance arrays with it; check and stratExit the fallback strategy; free on error paths.
fix_options.tested: Built 32- and 64-bit, 0 warnings; both reproducers clean under ASan/UBSan; clean under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL; check_scotch_graph_map/order/mesh_graph, check_prog_gmap/gpart pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Runs FM refinement on the new k-way mapping (intended). If the kgraph is a band graph the changed count is then caught by kgraphMapBd (GRA-20 fix). No ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Completes the intent stated by the existing :1047 comment; matches the surrounding 'read field, realloc, refill' idiom (cf. kgraphMapRb comploadavg realloc, kgraph_map_rb.c:169).

fix_options.label: Skip refinement when the fallback changed the part count
fix_options.summary: After the fallback, if grafptr->m.domnnbr != saved count (or fronnbr==0), free and return 0 (the fallback mapping is already valid).
fix_options.tested: Compiles; avoids the overflow by not entering the FM pass when the count changed.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Loses FM refinement exactly when the fallback created parts (quality, not correctness). Minimal and obviously safe.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He may prefer the refresh since the fallback was clearly meant to feed FM; this is the conservative fallback if refresh is judged risky.

cleanup_done: Removed the leak of the fallback Strat (now stratExit'd) and the ignored kgraphMapSt return; the const domnnbr becomes a mutable local that replaces all stale uses.
notes: Reachable from the default strategy only under imbalance with a frontier-less stage; the explicit 'rf{bal=...}' repro is the minimal public-API trigger.

our_title: FM edge-array growth publishes the new size before reallocating and callers ignore failure
ran: Injected an identical resize-failure hook (getenv GRA17_FAIL at the memRealloc call) into pristine and patched SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL libs (the only difference being the GRA-17 fix). Strategy 'm{vert=30,low=r{sep=h{pass=10}},asc=b{...f{...},org=f{...}}}' on 40x40/cmplt(64). Pristine: 'ERROR: kgraphMapFmEdgeResize: out of memory' then 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 ... kgraphMapFmPartAdd kgraph_map_fm.c:717 ... kgraphMapFm:1114'. Patched: FM returns the error cleanly with no overflow (a separate downstream mapTerm NULL-deref then appears, recorded as PS2-G13-1).
severity_note: Agrees with the review: the resize path is only reached under memory pressure (edxxsiz starts at 16x the frontier, capped at edgenbr); forced here with SCOTCH_DEBUG_KGRAPH2 + allocation injection.
evidence: 7.0.17 :524-525 `edxxsiz *= 2; *edxxsizptr = edxxsiz;` publishes the size before `memRealloc`; on failure it returns 1 but kgraphMapFmPartAdd/PartAdd2 ignore the result and `edxxidx = (*edxxnbrptr)++` writes into the un-grown array.
review_accuracy: Accurate. PartAdd/PartAdd2 are already int-returning (0), so only the two resize calls and the three top-level call sites needed changing.
first_pass_critique: Correct, and its diff matches what was committed (size published after success; both add routines return 1; three call sites checked). First pass also correctly noted the follow-on mapTerm NULL-load is a separate graphMapCompute2 weakness (here filed as PS2-G13-1).

fix_options.label: Publish size after success and propagate errors (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Move *edxxsizptr=edxxsiz after a successful memRealloc; make the two resize call sites return 1 on failure; check the three PartAdd/PartAdd2 call sites in kgraphMapFm and clean up.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; injection repro shows pristine overflow vs patched clean error chain; check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Pure error-path change; the new returns follow the local memFree(group-leader)+kgraphMapFmTablExit idiom already used by the out-of-memory (5)/(7) paths.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches his existing OOM handling in the same routine and the 'return 1 for cannot-allocate' convention.

fix_options.label: Pre-size the edge array to its worst case
fix_options.summary: Allocate edxxtab for edgenbr up front and delete kgraphMapFmEdgeResize, so no growth can fail.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Removes the failure mode but allocates the full edge count up front; the lazy doubling exists to avoid that memory cost.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Unlikely: he deliberately uses lazy doubling; he would rather handle the failure than regress memory.

notes: Shares kgraph_map_fm.c with GRA-02 but is an independent defect, so it is a separate commit.

our_title: Diffusion band-mapping thread with an isolated anchor skips the setup barriers, hanging the others
ran: Pristine 7.0.17 ASan (32-bit), gra12.c (two disjoint grids on cmplt(4), parts 2/3 empty -> isolated anchors), kgraphMapBd(bnd=d{pass=10}). 16 runs each: thr=2 4/16 hang, thr=3 6/16 hang, thr=4 5/16 hang (rc=124); also observed 'heap-use-after-free thread T6'. Patched: thr=2/3/4 all 0 hangs / 0 sanitizer reports over 16 runs; thr=8 clean.
severity_note: Agrees with the review: hang (DoS) on the default mapping strategy (asc=b{bnd=d{pass=40}...}) with threads enabled (SCOTCH_PTHREAD on), but only when an empty part yields an isolated anchor.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_map_df.c:224 & 230 (goto fail before the setup barriers at 257/288); also debug gotos at 180/208
evidence: 7.0.17: `if (velsmsk == 0) { loopptr->abrtval = 1; goto fail; }` (:222-225) and the sorttab OOM `goto fail` (:230) jump to the `fail:` label at :528, which is inside the pass loop AFTER both setup barriers; the aborting thread skips them while others wait forever. bgraph_bipart_df.c routes the same case through its barrier via `skip:`.
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the bgraph_bipart_df.c comparison. Only the empty-part isolated-anchor case is reachable (kgraphMapBd bails to the org strategy when an isolated anchor belongs to a non-empty part).
first_pass_critique: Status/method/evidence correct and the preferred option (fall through to the barriers) matches. But its sketch left the abort-path free as the pristine unconditional `memFree(sorttab)`, which crashes when a thread aborts before allocating (sorttab==NULL; memFreeRecord is not NULL-safe). The committed fix guards that free, as bgraph_bipart_df.c does for ielstax. First pass also missed the two SCOTCH_DEBUG_KGRAPH2 internal-error gotos (:180/:208) that have the same pre-barrier skip; they are fixed too.

extra_instances.quote: errorPrint ("kgraphMapDfLoop: internal error (1)"); loopptr->abrtval = 1; goto fail;

fix_options.label: Set abort flag and fall through to the existing barriers (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Replace the two pre-barrier `goto fail` with setting abrtval (no goto); guard the abort-path free; convert the two debug gotos to break+abort-after-barriers.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; 16 runs x {2,3,4} threads all clean; check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Reuses the two barriers already present and the existing `abrtval==1` exit; identical shape to bgraph_bipart_df.c's skip: handling. memFree(NULL) avoided by the guard.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Directly mirrors the twin routine bgraph_bipart_df.c (skip: label + guarded free), the strongest precedent.

fix_options.label: Reduce velsmsk across threads before the first barrier
fix_options.summary: Share-AND velsmsk into KgraphMapDfData and add a barrier so every thread decides identically, avoiding the private allocation entirely.
fix_options.tested: Not built (sketch; needs a new struct field).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Correct and avoids the sort-array allocation, but adds a shared field and a third barrier to a hot loop.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Heavier than the fall-through; he would prefer the minimal change that matches the existing twin.

cleanup_done: none needed (the `fail:` label stays, still used by the overflow gotos at 430/518)
notes: The harness's thread argument selects contextThreadSpawn(N) for N>1 else contextCommit (default thread count); both run multithreaded diffusion and both hit the bug.

our_title: Diffusion band mapping copies the part array from the stale buffer, lagging one pass
ran: Pristine 7.0.17 (32-bit), gra18.c kgraphMapBd(bnd=d{pass=N}) on a 2-part jagged 24x24 grid, counting changed vertices: pristine pass=21->1,22->1,23->2,24->7,25->8. Patched: pass=21->1,22->2,23->7,24->8,25->8 (patched[N]==pristine[N+1]: exactly one pass recovered).
severity_note: Agrees with the review: silent wrong (sub-optimal) result; a single-pass diffusion never changes the mapping. No crash.
evidence: 7.0.17 :525-527 swaps difntax/difotax at the end of each pass, so the freshest values are in difotax; :539 copies `difntax[vertnum].partval` (the pass-before-last). bgraph_bipart_df.c:398 reads difotax.
first_pass_critique: Fully correct; the one-line fix and the differential (original is one pass behind) match.

fix_options.label: Copy from difotax (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Read the last-written array (difotax) after the final swap.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; differential shows patched[N]==pristine[N+1]; robust for pass=0 too (difotax holds the initial parts); check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Changes diffusion results by one effective pass (typically slightly better); same array role as bgraph_bipart_df.c.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches the twin bgraph_bipart_df.c exactly (reads difotax after the swap).

fix_options.label: Swap only if another pass follows
fix_options.summary: Skip the final swap so difntax stays freshest and the copy stays as is.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Leaves the array roles different from bgraph_bipart_df.c; no advantage.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would prefer consistency with the twin, i.e. reading difotax.

our_title: kgraphCost isolated-anchor block is dead code; the review's fix to enable it is incorrect
ran: Pristine (32-bit) gra19.c (band graph around a 2-part cmplt(4) map, parts 2/3 empty): the block never runs, empty-part anchors get an average share (band avg 65 65 65 65). Making it live (review's fix) under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL with a default-style band map ('m{...asc=b{...}}') fires 'kgraphCost: invalid load difference' and then SEGVs; reverting only kgraph_cost.c removes the failure -> the live-fix is the cause. Recommended deletion build (32/64-bit) reproduces pristine exactly (band avg 65 65 65 65, sum(dlt)=0).
severity_note: Review rates low. The dead code is real but behaviour-neutral; the danger is in the review's suggested activation, not the current state.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_cost.c:150-172 (dead search loop + block), 177-180 (final load-target loop)
evidence: 7.0.17 :150-152 `for (...) if ((verttax[...+1]-verttax[...]) != 0) continue;` -- both outcomes continue, so domnnum always ends at domnnbr and the `if (domnnum != domnnbr)` block is unreachable; fdomwgt/fvelsum stay 0.
review_accuracy: Partly wrong. The dead code is real, but the review's fix ('== 0) break;') is incorrect: an anchor with no band edge is NOT a valid 'empty part' predicate -- after the band strategy repartitions, regular vertices can be assigned to a part whose anchor has no band edge, so freezing that part's load to the anchor weight subtracts a wrong value and trips the kgraphCost debug assertion (demonstrated).
first_pass_critique: The first pass correctly saw the review's one-word fix is insufficient and proposed break + skip-isolated-anchors-in-the-final-loop as preferred. But that 'make-live' variant is itself unsafe for the same reason (I reproduced 'invalid load difference' + SEGV under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL with it). The safe, honest resolution is to delete the dead block (behaviour-preserving), which the first pass only listed as the non-preferred option.

fix_options.label: Make the block live (break) and skip isolated anchors in the final loop
fix_options.summary: Turn the search into `==0) break;` and guard the final loop to skip isolated anchors.
fix_options.tested: Built; UNSAFE: under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL with a default-style band mapping it fires 'kgraphCost: invalid load difference' and SEGVs, because 'anchor has no band edge' is not equivalent to 'empty part' after repartitioning.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Would change balance targets for band graphs with such anchors, on a false premise; demonstrably breaks a debug invariant.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would NOT take this: it activates logic whose predicate is wrong and trips his own consistency check.

fix_options.label: Delete the dead block (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Remove the unreachable search loop and freeze block and the now-constant fdomwgt/fvelsum; behaviour is unchanged (the block never ran).
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; gra19 output identical to pristine; passes SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL and all check targets.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Zero behaviour change; removes misleading code. A correct freeze of truly-empty parts would need a proper empty-part test (a maintainer design decision).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He deletes code a change makes unused/misleading (STYLE); removing provably-dead code with a clear rationale is the honest action when the 'obvious' fix is wrong.

cleanup_done: Removed the unused `fdomwgt` (double) and `fvelsum` (Gnum) locals and simplified domnrat/velosum (no longer subtract the always-zero sums).
notes: A correct freeze of empty parts would need information kgraphMapBd has (vertnbrtab) but kgraphCost does not; flagged for the maintainer as a possible future improvement rather than attempted blindly.

our_title: Band mapping compares the part count with its own copy, never detecting a change; OOM path leaks
ran: Pristine (32-bit) gra20.c: 2-part map on cmplt(8), band strategy 'r{sep=h{pass=10}}' re-maps from scratch -> 'ret=0 changed=228 domnnbr=8' (silently accepted, part count corrupted 2->8). Patched: 'ERROR: kgraphMapBd: change in band graph number of parts not supported', ret=1, domnnbr=2.
read_only: the orgflagtab OOM leak path (line 268) is argued from the sibling failure paths; not exercised at runtime
why_not_run: The orgflagtab allocation-failure branch needs allocation-failure injection on that specific deep call; verified by inspection against the routine's two other failure paths which already free bndvnumtax + kgraphExit.
severity_note: Agrees with the review: logic error producing an inconsistent original graph; not a crash by itself.
evidence: 7.0.17 :181 `orggrafptr->m.domnnbr = bndgrafdat.m.domnnbr;` then :191 `if (bndgrafdat.m.domnnbr != orggrafptr->m.domnnbr)` compares a value with its own copy; the orgflagtab OOM at :268 returns without freeing bndvnumtax or exiting bndgrafdat.
review_accuracy: Accurate. Caveat (also noted): after the fix the previously-silent part-count change becomes an error, which is the documented 'not supported' contract and is consistent with the GRA-02 fallback inside a band graph.
first_pass_critique: Fully correct; the diff (compare against the entry-captured domnnbr, drop the premature overwrite, free on the OOM path) matches what was committed.

fix_options.label: Compare against the saved count; free on the OOM path (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Use the `domnnbr` local captured at entry, do not overwrite orggrafptr->m.domnnbr before the test, and add memFree(bndvnumtax)+kgraphExit on the orgflagtab failure.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; gra20 pristine ret=0/domnnbr=8 vs patched ret=1/domnnbr=2; check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: A band strategy that changes the part count now errors instead of continuing with inconsistent loads -- the documented 'not supported' behaviour.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The error message already says 'not supported'; the fix makes the guard actually enforce it, and the OOM free matches the routine's other two failure paths.

fix_options.label: Support a changed part count
fix_options.summary: Propagate the new count and resize/recompute the original graph's load arrays instead of erroring.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Real feature work: anchors and the comploaddlt memCpy assume equal counts; needs redesign and validation.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Against the routine's stated contract; he would reject a change of part count, not support it on the fly.

cleanup_done: Dropped the premature `orggrafptr->m.domnnbr = bndgrafdat.m.domnnbr;` assignment (no longer needed once the count is validated).
needs_note: Only the leak sub-case is un-run; the part-count defect is reproduced at runtime.

our_title: Upstream unsigned-shift fix missed the common.h bit-set macros used by the PT-Scotch bipartitioners
ran: UBSan on the exact macro expansion (standalone): pristine `(1 << 31)` -> 'runtime error: left shift of 1 by 31 places cannot be represented in type int'; fixed `(1U << 31)` -> clean. check_scotch_dgraph_check (PT-Scotch, 32-bit, mpirun -n 3) passes with the fix, 0 sanitizer reports.
read_only: the live PT-Scotch call site (bdgraphBipartEx/Bd flagging a ghost vertex whose based index is 31 mod 32) was not driven to that exact index
why_not_run: Hitting index == 31 mod 32 in the flag array needs an MPI run on a graph with >=32 such ghost/local vertices; the macro-level UBSan proof plus the source match to 6a00c51 establish it.
severity_note: Agrees with the review (undefined behaviour; compilers may miscompile). Reachable only in PT-Scotch band/exactifier bipartitioning with >=32 flagged vertices.
evidence: 7.0.17 common.h:321 `#define flagSet(a,n) (a)[(n)/(sizeof (int)<<3)] |= (1 << ((n)&((sizeof (int)<<3)-1)))` -- signed `int` array and `1 <<`; its users bdgraph_bipart_ex.c (movegsttab/flagloctab `int * restrict`) and bdgraph_bipart_bd.c (orgflagloctab `int *`) inherit the UB at bit 31.
upstream_change: 6a00c51 'Bugfix: apply left shifts to unsigned integers in bit sets [report R. Perry]' -- fixed hgraph_order_cp.c, hmesh_order_cp.c, kgraph_map_bd.{c,h}, library_dgraph_map_stat.c, mesh_induce_sepa.c but not common.h's flagSet/flagVal/flagSize.
review_accuracy: Accurate for 7.0.16 and the six listed files; the upstream fix for them is complete. The review's own list did not include common.h's generic flag macros, which remain the one residual instance.
first_pass_critique: First pass marked GRA-16 'fixed' but did (correctly) note the common.h flagSet/flagVal residual and the PT-Scotch users. Calling it simply 'fixed' understates it: the identical UB is still live in-tree via these macros. Correct status is partially-fixed, and the residual is fixed here.

extra_instances.quote: int * restrict movegsttab; int * restrict flagloctab; ... flagSize (...) * sizeof (int)

fix_options.label: Make the flag macros and their arrays unsigned (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Change flagSize/flagVal/flagSet to sizeof(unsigned int) and 1U<<, and the three flag arrays (movegsttab, flagloctab, orgflagloctab) to unsigned int, mirroring 6a00c51.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; macro UBSan clean; check_scotch_dgraph_check passes.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Matches exactly what 6a00c51 did for the kgraph_map_bd.h macros; no behaviour change (same bit patterns, defined now).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Literally the same transformation he applied in 6a00c51 to the twin macros in kgraph_map_bd.h -- the direct precedent.

fix_options.label: Minimal: only make the shift unsigned, keep int arrays
fix_options.tradeoffs: Removes the UB with a smaller diff but leaves signed arrays, diverging from the unsigned-array idiom 6a00c51 established.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He standardised on unsigned arrays in 6a00c51; a lone cast would be inconsistent with that commit.

notes: These common.h macros are the only remaining signed bit-set shift in the tree; a full grep of `1 << ` / `<<=` on signed operands reaching 31/63 found no other bit-set case (other hits are hypercube/arch dimensions and hash-table sizing with small, controlled shift counts).
